correctness.rationale: For each incomplete part V_i, an outside vertex has exactly |S|-|S cap V_i| neighbors in S, so 1-fairness is equivalent to |S|-s_i=1 on every incomplete part. Two incomplete parts force |S|<=2; one incomplete part forces all full parts together to have one vertex. These cases give the exact proper-set classification. The partition conclusions then follow directly. Exhaustive checking of all multipartite profiles and all set partitions through order 7 agrees with the theorem.

value.rationale: The fair coalition number was introduced recently and its partition behavior is not determined by the scalar fair-domination number. Complete multipartite graphs are a canonical test family, and the result reveals a sharp qualitative boundary: maximal singleton partitions on cliques and non-star bicliques, collapse to two blocks once a third part is present, and complete failure of partition existence exactly for nontrivial stars. The existence obstruction is also useful for clarifying when the newly defined parameter is actually realized.
